To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the innate immune response in mice to intratracheal administration of 1 μ g of purified, recom binant flagellin is characterized by the rapid production of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines, and the infiltration of neutro phils into the lungs.

the innate immune response in mice to intratracheally delivered flagellin was characterized by the rapid production of cytokines, chemokines, and neutrophils and by the induction of a protective adaptive immune response.

intratracheal administration of 1 μG of purified, recom- binant flagellin to several strains of mice induced a transient innate immune res- ponse characterized by the infiltration and accumulation of neutrophils in the air- ways and alveoli, the rapid production of cytokines and chemokines in the lung, and the recruitment and activation of alveolar macrophages and neutrophils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the innate immune response of mice to flagellin, a bacterial surface protein.
the innate immune system of the lung.
the development of novel vaccines and immunotherapies against infectious diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
flagellin is a strong inducer of innate immunity in the lung and that this response is dependent on the Toll-like receptor 5.
flagellin is a potent innate immunostimulatory molecule and that the innate immune system in the lung is capable of responding in a rapid and coordinated manner to a single immunostimulatory protein.
the flagellin-induced lung inflammation was a nonspecific innate response to a pathogen-associated molecular pattern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the flagellin-induced inflammatory response in the lung is dependent on the presence of the TLR5 receptor, and the response in the lung appears to involve both MyD88- and TRIF-dependent signaling pathways.
flagellin induces innate immunity in the mouse lung, which is dependent on the presence of TLR5, but not on the presence of other TLRs.
flagellin, a potent activator of the NF-κB pathway, is an excellent model molecule for the investigation of mucosal immunity and inflammation in the lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flagellin is an excellent model for studying the innate immune response in a mucosal organ, and that the response is dependent upon the presence of the flagellin receptor Toll-like receptor (TLR) 5.
the flagellin-based adjuvants are not only safe and immunogenic, but also have a favorable pharmacokinetic profile.
the flagellin gene can be used to develop a safe and effective vaccine against tuberculosis, and that this approach is likely to be useful for developing vaccines against other infectious diseases.
